payload.name: Count visits from place-anchored events
payload.description: When a question asks how many times a person has been to a specific city or country, and the memory evidence may describe actions that occurred there without using the word 'visit' or 'trip'.
content: Before answering a how-many-visits question, run a search that uses the place name itself (city and country) combined with the person's name, in addition to any literal 'visited <place>' query.

Count as a visit any distinct memory in which the person was present in that place, including receiving/giving something there, buying something there, attending an event there, or staying there; use the event date or world_start to separate distinct visits.
Stop expanding once the place-name search returns no new location-anchored events; do not enumerate every possible location synonym.

solves: Counting visits to a place fails when the only evidence is event memories that mention the place as the location of an action (e.g., received a gift, bought an item) rather than as a stated trip. The Skill applies to 'how many times has <person> been to <place>' questions where such place-anchored events exist; it must not be used when explicit visit/trip memories already answer the count, since the base retrieval is then sufficient.
